## Verdict: FAIL — one line still failing in part (RQ1 across a chain's segments); the other 25 lines fixed, pinned or REPORTED with their dependency; every gate green; the census held cell for cell; no other blocker

**The failing line — RQ1 (N-61 (1); item 130 (d), §3.6 step 4: "a chain's committed rows never retrace an edge").**
The round's cut is real and pinned for ONE SEGMENT's route (N-8's ring under `invisible` and under seven `way` keys
commit as simple paths; the there-and-back A–P–Q–P–R–B form is gone; this seat's mutants RQ1-cut, BACK, MAXCUT, GOON,
RETR all red — CONFIRMED). But `routed()` (insertChain.ts:889 – 903) opens a FRESH `SegmentPath` for every segment, and
step 3's contact filter (snapRound.ts:605 `onPath`, stretch.ts:771) excludes only the segment's own ends and the
segment's `exclude` set — so a vertex the chain's PREVIOUS segment routed through is an ordinary contact for the next
one, and the route goes back through it: a re-entry of "a vertex already on the chain's path" (the design's words) that
is neither cut nor refused. **Probe (mirror, `s9/probe/zzreenter.test.ts`, 8 of 8 run, CONFIRMED):** the framed 4 000 cm
square; an existing L0 `way` from W (2 030, 2 000) east to (3 500, 2 000); the mandatory chain A (2 500, 2 400) → V
(2 000, 2 000) → B (2 500, 1 600) — a plain three-point chain, its corner 77°, V 30 cm from W (beyond `attractCm`, so
step 2 leaves it free), each arm 18.8 cm from W (30 · sin 38.7°), so step 3 routes each arm through W. Under `invisible`
it COMMITS the rows A–W, W–V, W–B: W of degree 3 in the chain's row set, the chain's own corner V a dead end, warnings
`W_ATTRACTED ×2 at W, W_STRETCH_SHARED ×1 at V` (the second arm shares the chain's own edge V–W back to W — the retraced
edge); `allProblems` and `dissolvableProblems` empty, so nothing else catches it. Under a `way` key through M0-a-06's
transaction with the suite wired in (as the pipeline inserts) the batch is REFUSED `E_INVARIANT (way, way:c1) branches: a
linear role forms simple chains or rings (§3.10 role consistency)` — N-8's refusal class (the rulings' P1), one segment
later. The same in all four arrangements probed (W east or west of V, arms at ±38.7° and ±36.9°; W the dead end of a
`way` to the north). **In the registered families (the class-reading dump at the census seed 20261013, `s9/probe/out/`):**
of the constructive family's 10⁴ sequences, three well-separated simple three-point chains (every corner ≥ 60°, every
segment ≥ 60 cm, no two non-adjacent segments within 80 cm) commit with a branch in their own row set, each at an
existing vertex 28.9 – 30.4 cm from the chain's corner with the chain's spur to the corner: `way:3` L2 (1237, 474) (286,
846) (1688, 3058), branch at (315, 855) — the edges 286,846–315,855 `[way:3]`, 315,855–1107,553 `[way:2; way:3]`,
315,855–1546,2829 `[way:3]`; `way:6` L4 (1554, 2783) (1708, 3030) (3513, 470), branch at (1705, 3001); `way:2` L4
optional (1796, 1447) (1712, 1533) (478, 258), branch at (1705, 1505). Under a linear key each is a refusal of LAWFUL
input of our own making (J264 (2)) — a class the round neither fixed nor named (`refusalClass` names only the bound's
classes S – C; B-FUZZ's `ins` path runs no role consistency and has no simple-run oracle, so the census cannot see it);
under a non-linear role (`kerb`, `setback`, `invisible`) it is a committed row set that is not a simple run, which item
130 (d) says never commits. Not contrived: a chain corner 26 – 37 cm from an existing vertex inside the corner's wedge,
with both arms passing within `attractCm` of it. The line's own listed evidence passes (both fixtures, the mutant red,
the a-08 fixture PROPOSED) — the requirement it states does not.

**Required change (inside the item's owns):** the retrace rule applied to the CHAIN's path, not the segment's — the
vertices of the run's committed route so far (and the chain's landed points) carried into each `routeSegment` of the run
(`ChainCtx.path` / the `exclude` set `snapRound` starts from, or step 3's `onPath` reading the run's route) so that a
contact or landing on one is cut back to it as item 130 (d) says — where the cut would leave a landed input point off
the route (A–V–B's V), the reading goes on with that vertex excluded from step 3, as the per-segment code already does
(`placedBefore`), and the strict route (r2, contacts within `minEdge` only) then commits A–V–B as drawn (V–B passes 26 cm
from W: §3.10's clearance holds); pins in `test/insert/step3-5/`: the four arrangements above under `invisible` (every
vertex of the chain's row set of degree ≤ 2, no `W_STRETCH_SHARED` on the chain's own edge) and under a `way` key through
the transaction (the batch commits), and the three constructive cases of seed 20261013 above; the refusal census
re-measured after (never rising; the constructive family's count may fall by these commits' neighbours); the choices row
C-0423 (1) amended to say the cut is the chain's; a note if the session reads item 130 (d) otherwise (then the class is
named notBuilt by number with these cases).

Labels: every "CONFIRMED" below is an executed result in this seat's mirror or the tree; "PLAUSIBLE" is reasoned from
the code and the design text.
